**<mark>ICSG PRESS RELEASE                                            Date Issued: 21</mark>**<sup>**st**</sup> **<mark>October 2011</mark>** 



# **Copper: Preliminary Data for July 2011** 

The International Copper Study Group (ICSG) released preliminary data for July 2011 world copper supply and demand in its October 2011 Copper Bulletin. The Bulletin is available for sale upon request. 

According to preliminary ICSG data, the refined copper market balance for July 2011 showed a small production surplus of 18,000 metric tonnes (t). However, when making seasonal adjustments for world refined production and usage, July showed a surplus of 39,000 t. The apparent refined copper balance for the first seven months of 2011, including revisions to data previously presented, indicates a production deficit of 118,000 t (a seasonally adjusted surplus of 128,000 t). This compares with a production deficit of 329,000 t (a seasonally adjusted deficit of 70,000 t) in the same period of 2010. 

During the first seven months of 2011, world apparent usage grew by a modest 0.3% compared with that in the same period of 2010, as a 5% decline in Chinese apparent usage* mostly offset growth in other countries.  World usage without China grew by 4%, owing primarily to a significant increase in the Russian Federation apparent usage and also to some growth in the European Union (EU) and the United States. Growth in the United States and the EU, however, has weakened as the year has progressed.  Japanese usage, impacted by the earthquake/tsunami, was down by 2% as compared with that in the same period of 2010. On a regional basis, usage grew by 6% in Africa, 0.1% in the Americas, 10% in Europe, and 13% in Oceania, and declined by 3% in Asia (growth of 0.1% in Asia ex-China). 

During the first seven month of 2011, world mine production remained practically unchanged compared with production in the same period of 2010: Concentrate production grew by 0.1% and solvent extraction-electrowinning (SX-EW) by 0.9%. Production at three of the world’s four leading producers (Chile, Peru and the United States), that combined account for one half of the world’s production, was down by an aggregated 3.6%. However, production in China, currently the second leading producer, was up by 10%.  On a regional basis, mine production increased by 3% in Africa, 3% in Europe, and 13% in Oceania, but decreased by around 0.5% in the Americas and 4% in Asia.  The average mine capacity utilization rate for the first seven months of 2011 of 77.2% was 1.9% lower than that in the same period of 2010. 

During the first seven months of 2011 world refined production grew by 2.2% compared with that in the same period of 2010: Primary production increased by 0.6% and secondary production (from scrap) increased by 10%. Production increases of 32% in Australia (recovery from 2010 operational constraints), 15% in China, and 30% in the Democratic Republic of Congo were partially offset by declines in Chile

(-4.5%), the United Sates (-10%), Canada (-24%), and Japan (-18%). The average refinery capacity utilization rate for the first seven month of 2011 was practically unchanged from that in the same period of 2010 at 79%. Over an eight-day period in September 2011, the cash LME price fell by 21% from US$8,781.25 per tonne to US$6,975.50 per tonne, the lowest level since July 2010. The average LME cash price for September was US$8,314.84 per tonne, down from the August 2011 average of US$9,041.30 per tonne. The 2011 high and low copper prices through the end of September were US$10,148 and US$6,975.50 per tonne, respectively, and the average was US$9,253.98 per tonne. As of the end of September, copper stocks held at the major metal exchanges (LME, COMEX, SHFE) totalled 655,953 t, an increase of 87,771 t from stocks held at the end of December 2010. Compared to the August levels, stocks were up at LME and Comex and down at SHFE.
